criterion: A document is relevant if it is *devoted to* the topic of the query (the page a Python developer would want to open), not if it merely mentions the words. 'What's New' pages, indexes and glossary entries are not relevant. Labels were assigned from document titles and contents before any ranking was run.

queries.why: the event-loop reference, the conceptual overview, runners (which own the loop), the low-level API index, developing-with-asyncio, platform support of loops, the package overview
contextlib; the with statement; __enter__/__exit__ in the data model; 'Context Manager Types'
yield expressions; the yield statement; the Generators section of the functional HOWTO; the tutorial's Generators section
the Unicode HOWTO; unicodedata.normalize; NFKC normalization of identifiers
the reference; the FAQ 'How do I cache method calls?'
pickle and its security warning; shelve and marshal, which carry the same warning; the security-considerations page
FAQ 'Can't we get rid of the GIL?'; free threading; threading and the GIL; 'Thread State and the GIL' in the C API; thread safety of built-ins
the re reference and the regex HOWTO
the Sorting HOWTO; sorted(); list.sort(); the tutorial's list methods
the venv reference; the tutorial chapter; Installing Python Modules
random numbers and choices; secrets (cryptographically strong choices). The pages say 'random', 'choice', 'sample' — never 'by chance'.

queries.query: shrink data so it takes up fewer bytes
queries.why: the compression modules and the 'Data Compression and Archiving' index; they say 'compress', never 'shrink'.

queries.query: keep my objects on disk between program launches
queries.why: data persistence: pickle, shelve, dbm, marshal, sqlite3 and the 'Data Persistence' index; they say 'serialize', 'persistent', 'store'.
timing and profiling code: timeit, the profilers, perf profiling, time.perf_counter; they say 'execution time', 'profile', 'measure'.

queries.query: do several jobs at once on every core
queries.why: parallel execution: multiprocessing, concurrent.futures, interpreters, the concurrency index, free-threading; they say 'parallel', 'processes', 'concurrently' — not 'jobs at once'.

paraphrase_criterion: Lab 8: five queries that describe a topic in other words than the relevant pages use (their distinctive words — random, compress, pickle/persist, timeit/profile, parallel/process — are deliberately avoided). Labels were written before any run, by topic, like the original ten.
